finding: The kill-switch guard returns the bare router, unmounting js_tool_router() in full — which also carries the admin api_route /js-tool/settings, not only the JSON-RPC endpoint the defect names.
resolution: CONFIRMED by reading routes.rs, whose own module doc names both routes on line 2 — so my in-code justification ('js_tool's entire route surface IS the JSON-RPC endpoint') was factually false, and the guard was asymmetric with the split I deliberately applied to web_search/lit_search in the same commit. Split js_tool the same way: js_tool_router() keeps /js-tool/settings and always mounts; new js_tool_mcp_router() carries /run-js/mcp and is gated. Pinned by kill_switch_gate_test's settings-must-not-404 assertion.

finding: VoiceModule::new() flips enabled true->false, but voice already had both the unwrap_or(true) default and the register_routes guard upstream, so this hunk fixes no stated defect and is the exact shape the port must not carry (a default changed rather than a guard added).
resolution: CONFIRMED by reading upstream/main's voice/mod.rs:126-132 — register_routes already guards. REVERTED the file to upstream/main entirely; voice is now untouched by this branch. DESIGN_FIDELITY's INV-3 verdict amended: the fail-closed default applies to the three modules that GAIN the field, and voice is deliberately excluded rather than quietly included.

finding: The three kill-switch guards ship with no test; TestServerOptions has a voice_enabled knob and voice has a dedicated config_gate_test, but the security-shaped fix this branch is actually for has neither.
resolution: The most valuable finding of the round — a security fix with no proof is what B7 forbids. Added tests/mcp/kill_switch_gate_test.rs (4 tests, all passing) plus js_tool_enabled/web_search_enabled/lit_search_enabled knobs mirroring voice_enabled. Asserts 404-not-merely-non-200 on the JSON-RPC route (a non-200 assertion would pass against the ORIGINAL bug, which answered 403), NOT-404 on the settings route (the split), and a positive control that defaults leave everything mounted (without which the rest passes vacuously).

finding: The default_example() change is over-reach because 'no test requires it' — the conformance battery maps the absent-spec case to Ok(None) before any message assertion.
resolution: REJECTED, by running it rather than reasoning about it. Restored upstream/main's tools.rs and ran the test: `every_spawn_refusal_is_actionable` FAILS (panics at tools.rs:2018). So the change IS load-bearing and the finding's premise is wrong — the battery is not the only assertion; tools.rs:1904-1915 separately demands the message contain default_example(). Change kept. This is why an oracle beats an argument.

finding: CHAT_STREAM_CONNECTION_HEADER is made pub and re-exported so allowlists 'can reference the constant instead of re-spelling the literal', but the production allowlist still re-spells it; only the unit test uses the constant.
resolution: Correct and embarrassing — the stated rationale for widening a public API was not realised at the one call site it was widened for. The desktop allow_headers vec now uses ziee::CHAT_STREAM_CONNECTION_HEADER.

finding: The claim, repeated in downloads.rs, that this 'was the ONLY SSE endpoint without' keep-alive is false: code_sandbox/streaming.rs:250 returns a bare Sse::new(stream).
resolution: CONFIRMED by grep. Same defect class this branch's ITEM-11 fixes elsewhere — a comment asserting a tree-wide invariant that does not hold. Both comments corrected; code_sandbox's stream is left alone (it is bounded by a single command rather than idling indefinitely) but the sweep is explicitly no longer claimed complete.

finding: The llm_repository test/doc repair is legitimate but is not named in the stated defect list, so it arrives as undeclared scope in a port whose premise is 'port the defect fix only'.
resolution: Fair, and the shape is deliberate rather than accidental: it is ITEM-11, added to PLAN.md after the audit found the tests RED on upstream/main, and kept as its OWN commit precisely so the owner can drop it independently of the ports. The PR body says so. Declaring it is the fix; removing it would leave a repo's own suite red when the fix is five lines.

finding: MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0 raises the pgvector extension's macOS runtime floor from 10.13 to 11.0 while no minimumSystemVersion is declared in the bundle config, so a 10.15 host gets a bundle that installs and then fails at first migration.
resolution: Real and worth knowing, but NOT actionable here: without the raise, pgvector does not COMPILE on macOS against PG18 at all (PG18's pg_iovec.h uses preadv/pwritev under -Werror=unguarded-availability-new), so the alternative to an 11.0 floor is no working macOS build. Declaring minimumSystemVersion is a packaging decision for the owner, on a platform this box cannot build for. Surfaced in the PR body rather than silently changed.

finding: The forwarder writes every GitProgress frame verbatim including the LFS scan frame (current 0, total 0), and since the first observation is never withheld it immediately overwrites the 'Checking for LFS files… 20/100' record with 0/0.
resolution: Plausible and specific, and it describes CODE THAT ALREADY SHIPS IN PAWS — this is a faithful port, not a defect introduced here. Not fixed in this PR: changing the forwarder's frame filtering is new design work on a module whose behaviour paws has in production, and doing it blind (no rootfs, no multi-GB LFS repo, and squashfuse absent on this box) would be guessing. REPORTED to the owner for a paws-side branch where it can be reproduced. The pre-existing 0-100-scale writes it interacts with (uploads.rs:1169/1249/1329) are likewise pre-existing.

finding: With a 1s throttle and the first-write-always rule, a fast LFS step (cached object, hard-linked rather than transferred) emits only the 0/0 scan write and throttles away every later frame including the terminal one.
resolution: Same disposition and same reason as the row above: ships in paws today, needs a reproducible LFS transfer to verify or fix, and the environment here cannot provide one. Reported rather than guessed at.

finding: phase is hardcoded to DownloadPhase::Downloading for every frame, so LfsPhase::Error and LfsPhase::Complete frames persist as in-flight downloading progress with placeholder counters.
resolution: Same family, same disposition — pre-existing in paws, reported.

finding: The DB write is awaited inside the recv loop, so the unbounded channel can still grow whenever a single update_progress is slow.
resolution: Correct that the buffer is unbounded, but this is a large improvement on the defect being fixed (where NOTHING drained it, so it grew for the whole transfer by construction rather than only during a DB stall). Bounding it is a further change to shipped paws code; reported, not attempted here.

finding: The test and the production comments claim a user could POST /api/run-js/mcp and 'execute arbitrary script', but js_tool's tools/call arm explicitly refuses to execute — it serves only initialize/tools_list/ping, and the real execution gate is the chat extension.
resolution: CONFIRMED by reading js_tool/handlers.rs:64-70, which returns an error for tools/call with the message 'run_js must be invoked in a chat context; it is executed inline by the chat runtime, not over the loopback transport'. My headline security claim was OVER-BROAD for js_tool. Also checked the siblings: web_search/handlers.rs:80 and lit_search/handlers.rs:76 DO dispatch tools/call, so the egress claim holds for those two. Corrected in js_tool/mod.rs, js_tool/routes.rs, the test header and the commit message, stating the severity PER MODULE rather than flattening it. Note tinnlab/paws 816aa6321 makes the same over-broad claim.

finding: The doc says 'The user is created with NO permissions on purpose', but create_user_with_permissions(.., &[]) registers via /auth/register which places the user in the default group, so it holds the *::use grants.
resolution: Correct, and it inverts the stated rationale: a mounted route would SERVE this caller (200), not refuse it (403) — which makes the 404 assertions STRONGER than I claimed, not weaker. Rewritten, with an explicit warning not to 'tighten' the assertions to assert_ne!(403) on the false premise.

finding: The tree now encodes two opposite kill-switch contracts: this branch's test requires the settings REST to STAY mounted for three modules, while voice unmounts its whole surface and tests/voice/config_gate_test.rs asserts /voice/settings MUST be 404.
resolution: Real, and deliberately NOT resolved here. Unifying them means changing voice's behaviour — the exact out-of-scope drift round 1 just reverted — and picking which policy wins is a product decision for the owner. Recorded prominently in the test file's header so whoever unifies them knows both tests exist and one must move.

finding: The six route-path literals are duplicated between the disabled tests and the positive control rather than shared, so a typo in one disabled test would make its 404 assertion pass for the wrong reason while the control still passes.
resolution: A maintenance hazard rather than a live defect — the auditor verified all six literals are correct today against the three routes.rs files. Left as-is deliberately: sharing them via constants would couple the test to the router module and make the paths less legible at the assertion site, and the positive control already fails loudly if a real path moves. Recorded so the tradeoff is visible.

finding: After the revert, VoiceModule::new() defaults enabled:true while the three other modules fail closed with false and carry comments arguing why fail-closed is required for a kill switch.
resolution: Accurate, and the asymmetry is the PRICE of round 1's revert — which was itself the right call (changing voice fixes no defect this branch names). Currently benign: voice/mod.rs:101 assigns self.enabled before any early return and nothing fallible precedes it. Reported to the owner alongside the contradictory-contracts finding, since both are resolved by the same decision about what a kill switch should mean.
